title: The book sale
body: A rainy Saturday, a library book sale and one battered copy of The Left Hand of Darkness. We both reached for it. Ezra let Maren have it, then spent an hour "accidentally" browsing the same tables. She lent it back to him three weeks later, with notes in the margins.

title: The first trip
body: Four days, one tent and a borrowed car with no working radio. We learned that Maren navigates by snacks and Ezra cannot walk past a tide pool. It rained for three of the four days and we still call it the best trip we have taken.

title: One apartment, two desks
body: We moved in together a month before the world shut down, so the apartment got a very thorough test. Two desks in one bedroom, a rooftop with one folding chair, and a lot of sourdough. We came out of it sure of one thing.

title: Enter Biscuit
body: Biscuit is a mostly-beagle who came home from the shelter for "a two-week trial". She is now four, has her own Instagram that nobody asked for, and will be walking down the aisle with a very small bow tie.

title: The question
body: Ezra planned a sunrise canoe trip and was so nervous he forgot the paddles. By the time we borrowed some it was nearly eight, the mist had gone and the ring had been in his pocket for two hours. Maren said yes before he finished the question.

title: Why Willowbank
body: Maren's grandparents picked apples at Willowbank every October for forty years. When we went to see it, the old trees were in blossom and the barn smelled of cider. We booked it that afternoon. We can't wait to share it with you.
